sections.section_goal: World models that learn compact dynamics for game-like or interactive environments.

selected_papers.title: World Models
selected_papers.problem: How to learn compact spatial and temporal representations of game environments so that agents can train with fewer direct environment interactions.
selected_papers.method: A variational autoencoder compresses observations, an MDN-RNN predicts latent dynamics, and a compact controller is optimized in latent space.
selected_papers.contribution: The paper showed that agents can be trained inside learned models of game environments such as CarRacing and VizDoom.
selected_papers.limitations: The demonstrations use relatively simple environments, and accumulated rollout error can weaken long-horizon planning.
selected_papers.selection_reason: Matches game / agent / world model keywords with strong relevance.

selected_papers.title: Diffusion World Models
selected_papers.problem: How to use diffusion-style generative modeling for world dynamics and agent learning.
selected_papers.method: The work uses diffusion models to represent or predict environment dynamics for model-based learning.
selected_papers.contribution: It expands the design space of generative world models beyond recurrent latent dynamics.
selected_papers.limitations: Diffusion rollouts can be expensive and must be assessed for temporal consistency.
selected_papers.selection_reason: Matches game / agent / world model keywords with strong relevance.

selected_papers.title: GAIA-1: A Generative World Model for Autonomous Driving
selected_papers.problem: How to learn a controllable generative world model for complex embodied environments.
selected_papers.method: GAIA-1 models video, action, and scene context to generate plausible future driving observations.
selected_papers.contribution: Although outside games, it shows how controllable world models can transfer to high-stakes embodied simulation.
selected_papers.limitations: Driving-focused results do not directly solve game intelligence evaluation and require domain-specific validation.
selected_papers.selection_reason: Matches game / agent / world model keywords with strong relevance.

selected_papers.title: Grandmaster Level in StarCraft II Using Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
selected_papers.problem: How to train agents for a complex real-time strategy game with partial observability and long-horizon decisions.
selected_papers.method: AlphaStar combines supervised learning, reinforcement learning, and league-based multi-agent training.
selected_papers.contribution: The work demonstrated grandmaster-level performance in StarCraft II and highlighted the value of competitive training ecosystems.
selected_papers.limitations: The system relies on extensive engineering, training scale, and domain-specific interfaces.
selected_papers.selection_reason: Matches game / agent / world model keywords with strong relevance.

selected_papers.title: Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior
selected_papers.problem: How to create believable interactive agents that remember, plan, and act in a simulated social environment.
selected_papers.method: The system combines memory streams, reflection, planning, and language-model-driven action selection.
selected_papers.contribution: It illustrated how generative agents can populate interactive worlds with coherent behavior.
selected_papers.limitations: Behavioral realism and evaluation remain difficult, and language-model outputs need guardrails.
selected_papers.selection_reason: Matches game / agent / world model keywords with strong relevance.

sections.section_title: Planning and Control with Learned Models
sections.section_goal: Agents that use learned dynamics for planning, control, or policy learning.

selected_papers.title: DreamerV3: Mastering Diverse Domains through World Models
selected_papers.problem: How to make world-model reinforcement learning robust across diverse domains with minimal task-specific tuning.
selected_papers.method: DreamerV3 learns a latent world model and trains actor-critic behavior from imagined trajectories.
selected_papers.contribution: It broadened the empirical case for world-model agents across visual control and game-like domains.
selected_papers.limitations: The approach still depends on learned model quality and careful evaluation across domains.
selected_papers.selection_reason: Matches game / agent / world model keywords with strong relevance.

selected_papers.title: Mastering Atari, Go, Chess and Shogi by Planning with a Learned Model
selected_papers.problem: How to combine planning with learned dynamics without requiring a hand-coded simulator model.
selected_papers.method: MuZero learns representation, dynamics, and prediction functions and uses tree search over the learned model.
selected_papers.contribution: The system achieved strong results in Atari and classic board games while learning the model used for planning.
selected_papers.limitations: The planning machinery and training pipeline are computationally demanding.
selected_papers.selection_reason: Matches game / agent / world model keywords with strong relevance.

sections.section_title: Neural Game Engines and Interactive Environments
sections.section_goal: Generative systems that synthesize controllable interactive environments.

selected_papers.title: Genie: Generative Interactive Environments
selected_papers.problem: How to learn action-controllable interactive environments from video-scale data.
selected_papers.method: Genie learns a latent action model and video generator to create controllable environments from visual examples.
selected_papers.contribution: It connected generative video modeling with interactive environment construction for agents and players.
selected_papers.limitations: Generated environments require careful evaluation of controllability, temporal coherence, and task semantics.
selected_papers.selection_reason: Matches game / agent / world model keywords with strong relevance.

selected_papers.title: GameNGen: Diffusion Models Are Real-Time Game Engines
selected_papers.problem: How to generate interactive game frames in real time using learned generative dynamics.
selected_papers.method: The system uses a diffusion model conditioned on previous frames and actions to produce playable game-video dynamics.
selected_papers.contribution: It framed diffusion models as neural game engines capable of interactive visual simulation.
selected_papers.limitations: Real-time generative play raises consistency, controllability, and evaluation challenges.
